question: A 26-year-old patient with no prior medical-surgical history came to the emergency room for dyspnea of ​​15 days of evolution. No findings of interest were detected on the physical examination except a nodule of hard consistency in the left testicle. A chest x-ray is performed, showing multiple pulmonary nodules in "balloon release". His analytical highlights a B-hCG of 30,000 mIU / ml. What do you think is the most probable origin of the pathology of this picture?
